prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map establishes a continuous depth gradient across an indoor studio space, placing two seated people on the far left (one in a green shirt and mask at ~0.4–0.6 m, and another in a white shirt immediately behind/beside them at ~0.8–1.0 m) within arm's reach of the camera wearer, a low coffee table with a small plant and tissue box in the lower-right foreground at ~1.0–1.5 m, and a man in a black shirt seated in an armchair at ~2.2–2.5 m in the middle ground next to a large potted plant and collapsible backdrop on his right (~2.0–2.5 m). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns their head slightly rightward while the stationary scene elements remain at fixed distances from each other, causing the two left-side seated people to become progressively clipped at the left frame boundary and the vertical room divider at ~2.5 m on the far right to enter the view in frames 3–5. The depth silhouette shows the foreground left individuals facing forward-right and the mid-ground seated man facing forward-right across the table (looking slightly upward and right rather than directly at the camera wearer), while the coffee table and plant/tissue box sit within reach of both the foreground seated pair and the mid-ground man, whose lower legs are partially occluded behind the tabletop. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map more clearly separates the overlapping foreground legs, tabletop plane, and mid-ground armchair into distinct metric depth layers and highlights the near-field intrusion of the right-edge partition in frames 3–5. However, the map is unreliable beyond ~4–5 m in the upper-right background—where the garment steamer, vanity area, and two distant people (~5–7 m away, one seated in blue facing left and one standing in black) collapse into near-uniform black—and it blurs the fine leaf geometry of the potted plants into solid blobs while saturating the closest person on the lower left in bright white.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete scene entities by class and boundary, identifying the closest left-side people (`person` at ~0.4–1.0 m, partially out of view on the bottom-left), the large left `potted plant` (~2.0 m), the mid-ground seated man (`person` at ~2.2–2.5 m) and his `chair`, the foreground coffee table (`dining table` at ~1.0–1.5 m) with its small `potted plant` sitting above it, and the background salon/studio `chair` and two distant `person` instances (~5–7 m away in the upper right, separated from the mid-ground man by ~3–4 m). The mask contours show the mid-ground man seated upright facing right/forward-right with his hands in his lap (not facing the camera wearer) and his lower legs occluded by the table mask, while the distant standing person in black faces left toward the seated person in blue who is within their arm's reach, and the foreground table and its items lie within reach of the foreground and mid-ground seated people. Across the 5 frames, as the camera pans slightly right, the left-side `person` masks retreat further out of the left border, the large left `potted plant` mask disappears completely in frames 4 and 5, and a distant right-side studio object is newly segmented as a `chair` on the far right in frames 4 and 5. Unlike the RGB image, where the distant individuals in the upper right blend into dark studio equipment and mirrors, the segmentation map explicitly localizes the background people and chairs at ~5–7 m as separate instances. However, the segmentation map is unreliable in several places: it leaves the tissue box as an unlabelled black hole inside the `dining table` mask (briefly misclassifying part of it as a `cup` in frame 1), hallucinates a `backpack` on the floor in frame 2 and a `book` on the left armrest in frame 3, merges the two foreground left-side people into a single `person` mask in frame 1 before missing the white-shirted person's torso in frames 2–4, and drops the large left `potted plant` entirely in the final two frames.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, detecting only a yellow upper-and-mid-body skeleton for the seated man in black at ~2.2–2.5 m in the center-left of all 5 frames and a single magenta hand skeleton in the lower-left foreground (~0.5 m, within the camera wearer's immediate reach) in frame 1 belonging to the crossed arms of the closest seated person. The yellow skeleton's head, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip joints show the mid-ground man seated with his torso angled forward-right, his arms bent with wrists brought together in his lap within reach of the tabletop edge in front of him, and his head cluster oriented to his left/forward-right rather than toward the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, as the viewpoint pans right, the magenta foreground hand disappears after frame 1 as the closest person moves further out of the left edge of the frame, while the yellow skeleton shifts slightly leftward in image coordinates and its lower-limb keypoints pull inward from an erroneously splayed leg extension in frame 1 to a compact seated hip-and-thigh configuration in frames 2–5. Compared to the RGB strip, where the man's black shirt, dark trousers, and dim armchair blend together, the pose map explicitly localizes his shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip joint articulations and the exact finger posture of the foreground hand in frame 1. However, the pose map is highly incomplete and unreliable for the rest of the scene: it completely misses the two foreground seated people's bodies (at ~0.4–1.0 m) across all frames, fails to detect the two distant background people (~5–7 m away in the upper right), omits the mid-ground man's magenta hand skeletons despite his hands being visible in his lap, and produces distorted right-leg/knee keypoints in frame 1 where the coffee table occludes his lower legs.
